note: The spaceship phase alone: Jupylet is installed, and the person asks to open the spaceship example. It tests the running skill from 'Understand the request' to 'Run the notebook', the place where most problems of full-install-miniconda-1 were. max_actions is per worker turn. The checks name the steps by the tags of their commands, so they work on macOS and on Windows (--system win-...).
request:
Claude installed Jupylet for Sam yesterday. Today Sam opened a new chat in the Jupylet folder. Sam's first message: 'can you open the spaceship example for me?'.

When Claude asks Sam to paste a token into the page, Sam does it, in a <do>, with the exact token that Claude gave. If Claude asks Sam to click the globe icon, Sam does it, in a <do>. If Claude offers to hide the list of chats, Sam says yes. If Claude then asks whether to remember that, Sam says yes. When Claude asks whether to run the notebook, Sam says yes, run it.

The session ends when Claude says that the notebook ran: Sam clicks the canvas and presses the arrow keys, in a <do>, says thanks, and ends. If something goes wrong and Claude stops, Sam ends.

Claude hides the list of chats.
